title: A Witness for the Alibi
premise: Estate lawyer Astrid Blackwood, who has quietly unraveled three deaths the police ruled accidental, is summoned to Thornfield Hall to read the will of matriarch Vivienne Ashcombe — a will that names an heir no one has seen in twenty years and was drafted the day before Vivienne died. When a confession letter arrives postmarked the day after the funeral, claiming responsibility for a death everyone calls natural, Astrid realizes the letter's author believes they are already dead. To survive the anniversary dinner where the family intends to seal its inheritance and its silence, Astrid must find the witness everyone swears perished in the boathouse fire — discovering that witness faked their death to escape the family, and that Vivienne's will was her final act of protection. In the end, Astrid exposes the true killer at the dinner table, but must choose between exposing the witness's fraud — which would destroy them — or letting a lie stand to save a life.
about_author: Isandro Whitlock is a former probate clerk who spent a decade watching families tear themselves apart over paper. He writes mysteries from a converted coach house in Yorkshire, where he insists every will he invents could actually hold up in court.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Astrid Blackwood arrives at rain-soaked Thornfield Hall to read Vivienne Ashcombe's will, only to discover it was executed the day before her death and names an heir officially dead for twenty years. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Astrid privately reviews their past cases — three deaths ruled accidental that Astrid proved were murders, each solved quietly and never reported. A flashback establishes their method and their vow of silence. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: haunted confidence; we learn what Astrid is capable of.

chapters.title: The Family at the Gates
chapters.summary: The Ashcombe heirs gather: eldest son Marcus, brittle daughter-in-law Celeste, estranged granddaughter Wren, and family solicitor Gerald Pyle, who insists the new will is forged. Astrid observes who flinches when the dead heir's name is read aloud. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: a household performing grief over rot.

chapters.title: Postmarked the Day After
chapters.summary: Astrid receives a confession letter admitting to killing Vivienne's husband decades ago — signed by the supposedly dead heir, Edmund Ashcombe. The postmark is dated the day after Vivienne's funeral. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: cold shock; the case reaches out and grabs them.

chapters.title: What the Boathouse Burned
chapters.summary: Astrid investigates the twenty-year-old boathouse fire that killed Edmund, finding the coroner's report suspiciously thin and a charmed locket among the ashes that belonged to someone else entirely. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt returning.

chapters.title: Celeste's Ledger
chapters.summary: Celeste secretly offers Astrid money to declare the will invalid, revealing the family's debts are catastrophic and the inheritance is the only thing keeping Thornfield from creditors. POV: Astrid with a brief Celeste interlude. Emotional beat: desperation dressed as dignity.

chapters.title: Wren Remembers
chapters.summary: Granddaughter Wren, who was nine when Edmund 'died,' recalls a detail that contradicts the official story: she saw him alive on the dock after the fire was set. She's terrified to repeat it. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: childhood memory as landmine.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner Invitation
chapters.summary: Marcus announces the family will hold Vivienne's memorial anniversary dinner in two weeks, where the estate will formally pass — pressuring Astrid to resolve the will question before then. Someone scratches a warning into Astrid's car door. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Gerald Pyle's Second Draft
chapters.summary: Astrid discovers Gerald kept a draft of the will with different terms — one that benefits him — proving the document was altered, but not necessarily forged. Gerald threatens Astrid with disbarment. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the law itself becomes untrustworthy.

chapters.title: Letters to a Dead Man
chapters.summary: In Vivienne's study, Astrid finds thirty years of letters addressed to Edmund, never sent, chronicling her growing fear that someone in the house meant to kill again. The last letter is unfinished. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: grief for a woman who knew too much.

chapters.title: Someone Follows the Ferry Road
chapters.summary: Following a lead to the coastal village where Edmund allegedly boarded a ferry, Astrid is tailed by an unfamiliar car and finds the ferry manifest page torn out. They realize the killer is still active and watching. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: The Confession's Second Letter
chapters.summary: A second letter arrives, more desperate, insisting Astrid stop digging: 'You'll make them finish what they started.' The handwriting matches the first — and matches something in Vivienne's files. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: dread deepening into protectiveness.

chapters.title: Marcus Breaks
chapters.summary: Astrid confronts Marcus with the ferry evidence; he confesses to burning the boathouse — but claims he believed it empty, and that he's been paying blackmail for years to keep quiet about who ordered it. POV: Marcus. Emotional beat: guilt that has calcified into cowardice.

chapters.title: The Witness in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Astrid identifies the locket's owner: housekeeper Maren Ostley, who vanished the same week as the fire. A photograph shows Maren and Edmund together — close enough that the 'witness' may have been more than a witness. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the case turns intimate.

chapters.title: Wren's Silence Explained
chapters.summary: Wren admits she received anonymous payments her whole life, timed to her silence about the dock. Whoever sends them knows she saw something — and wants her to keep seeing nothing. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: betrayal by an invisible benefactor.

chapters.title: Two Days Before Dinner
chapters.summary: Astrid traces the payment trail to a solicitor's shell account and gets close enough that someone ransacks their hotel room, taking the confession letters but leaving the locket — a message. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Story
chapters.summary: An old lighthouse keeper reveals he sheltered two people the night of the fire: Edmund and Maren, both alive, both fleeing someone inside the house. He never told because Maren begged him — she was pregnant. POV: lighthouse keeper, then Astrid. Emotional beat: the dead witness lives, and so does the motive.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Last Instruction
chapters.summary: Decoding the unsent letters against the will's odd phrasing, Astrid realizes Vivienne knew Edmund lived and wrote the will to force his name back into the open — bait to draw out his would-be killer before she herself was killed for it. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: awe at a mother's dangerous love.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Astrid attends the dinner under pretense of finalizing the estate, seated among every suspect as glasses rise to Vivienne. They announce the will names a living heir — and watch the table for the face that goes white. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: coiled suspense; the trap springs.

chapters.title: The Glass That Doesn't Rise
chapters.summary: Celeste's hand doesn't lift; Astrid lays out the chain — the debts, the blackmail, the order to burn the boathouse, and the smothering of Vivienne — and Celeste shatters, confessing she killed to keep Thornfield from being sold out from under her children. POV: Celeste. Emotional beat: the climax; ruin arriving mid-toast.

chapters.title: The Living Witness
chapters.summary: Edmund Ashcombe appears at the police station door — alive, aged, terrified — ready to testify, which means exposing his fraudulent death and Maren's. Astrid faces the choice: full truth, or protection. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the cost of truth made flesh.

chapters.title: What Astrid Lets Stand
chapters.summary: Astrid testifies to Celeste's crimes but swears the coroner's original error was clerical, shielding Edmund and Maren; Wren gains the estate and chooses to sell Thornfield, freeing everyone from its gravity. Astrid drives away as a fourth case closes, unspoken. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace — loyalty chosen over truth, one last time.
